findings.desc: Scope-shrinkage confirmation is not mechanically aligned with the decision doc. The doc requires a scope-shrinkage decision with userConfirmed:true and says reviewer/agent judgment is not enough (docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-intent-collision-execution-plan.md:480-496), but the shipped command/data model only records decision, removedMilestoneIds, reason, and approvedBy, with approvedBy documented as human or agent and no userConfirmed field (packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2071-2077; packages/main/src/core/types.ts:1889-1895). DONE equivalence then treats any decision=confirmed as accepted shrinkage and skips those milestones (packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:986-988,1010-1012). This lets an agent-authored shrinkage artifact satisfy DONE intent equivalence for a narrower outcome, contrary to the documented user-confirmation gate.

M4/M9 ProofStory DEV enforcement is not covered on rollback/re-entry and appears bypassable. packages/main/src/core/config.ts:53 documents devGateMode as covering PLAN/INIT_CHECK/REVIEW rollback DEV admission, but packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:579 implements canReenterDevGuard with only the parallelDevEntryBlock check and no proofStoryDevGateFailure call. The guard-failure path likewise skips ProofStory for rollback because packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:982 only evaluates proofStoryDevGateFailure when !isRollbackDoor. The current smoke verifies direct proofstory_gate_check enforce failure at packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.ts:279 and that diagnostics do not advance phase at packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.ts:335, but it never exercises story_advance DEV from REVIEW/TEST under proofStory.devGateMode=enforce. A story can therefore pass the smoke/build/process-fact evidence while the lifecycle policy gate is absent on a documented DEV entry path.

The ProofStory execution plan command/artifact inventory does not match the implemented CLI surface. The doc lists current New Commands that are not registered or implemented, including intent_collision_start/record/resolve, acceptance_contract_set/acceptance_criterion_add/acceptance_evidence_bind, red_evidence_validate, minimality_check_set/minimality_alternative_record, risk_classify, and assurance_level_set (docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-intent-collision-execution-plan.md:950-993), while the catalog exposes the implemented ProofStory commands without those names and adds proofstory_review_completeness_check instead (packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:2026-2156). The Storage section also calls intent-coverage-check.json, done-intent-equivalence.json, acceptance-contract.json, and minimality-check.json new gate-consumed artifacts (docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-intent-collision-execution-plan.md:1026-1042), but the store only persists original-intent-snapshot.json, milestone-ledger.json, proofstory.json, intent-collision.json, scope-shrinkage-decision.json, red-evidence.json, and spike.json (packages/main/src/core/store.ts:655-743), and the coverage/equivalence/check handlers are read-only diagnostics (packages/main/src/handlers/proofstory.ts:391-420). This leaves the requirements doc as a misleading operator/spec source for command names and gate evidence.

ProofStory is specified as a pre-DEV contract layer: M3 requires PLAN-only mutation policy for intent_collision_set, M4/M6/M7 require the gate/red/spike artifacts to block before DEV in enforce mode, and the gate outputs say incomplete ProofStory work should stay in PLAN. The implementation registers the core ProofStory artifact writers as story-scoped gate evidence but allows them in DEV in both command-policy and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS: original_intent_snapshot_set, milestone_ledger_set/add, proofstory_contract_set, intent_collision_set, red_evidence_create, and spike_* can all be written after implementation has started. That lets agents backfill or revise the intent/collision/contract/red/spike record during DEV instead of proving it before DEV, weakening the M0-M9 conceptual boundary even though the diagnostics themselves are pure and do not create a second lifecycle state machine. Narrow these pre-DEV artifact writers to INIT/PLAN as appropriate, leaving only explicit scope-shrinkage/DONE-time decisions in later phases, and update phase allowlist plus command policy together. Source refs: packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts:356, :358, :361, :363, :367, :369; packages/main/src/core/config.ts:304, :325; docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-intent-collision-execution-plan.md:1144, :1165, :1210, :1227.
